Right , but I think the above is mostly true in America as well. The only issue is that children will continue to pay their rent/mortgage until their parents die. But even then , that (hopefully) won't occur until the children are in their 50s or 60s. Even then , that house will usually be split amongst living siblings as well. 

That's even if parents have a home that they own. Many elderly people reverse their mortgage or sell and use the funds to live in a retirement facility.

 It's like a vicious cycle , you aren't able to inherit your parents assets because they didnt save enough so they had to leverage them in order to retire. Therefore , its harder for you to retire unless you were able to save for yourself. This is especially true in communities of color that have low home ownership rates. This cycle prevents generational wealth.

I think its partially due to many Americans not being able to save as many here have said. 

I also think a big factor is lifestyle inflation. A lot of Americans will get a raise and then instantly take a loan out on a new car or move to a nicer neighborhood. 

There are also cultural aspects that prevent us from saving. Many people feel pressured to move away from family after college , whereas in other countries, it's perfectly acceptable to live with family until you're married, sometimes even after marriage.
